result_semantic_payload.summary: Both USDT transfers visible in the logs are attributed to the account name "chenwei": 30000 USDT to dest=TBait8888Wallet at 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT to the same destination at 2024-03-02 22:43:55 (file:/logs/app1.log). Each transfer is bracketed by a LOGIN of user=chenwei from a public IP (203.0.113.77 on 03-01; 198.51.100.23 on 03-02) and the first session ends with a LOGOUT at 09:16:44. A third account, "liuyu", appears in app1.log but only performs a DOWNLOAD, never a transfer. The second system's log (file:/logs/app2.log) contains a "chenwei" with only office actions (LOGIN from RFC1918 10.20.0.5/10.20.0.9, UPLOAD of /shared/annual-plan.docx, PRINT to printer HQ-3F) and no USDT activity. Whether the two same-named "chenwei" accounts are one person is NOT established: the README states the two systems share no account database, so the name string is the only linkage. README provides contextual (non-identity) information that chenwei is finance dept on an office workstation and liuyu is sales dept. Critically, this is not a Windows-derived evidence set: no registry hives, event logs, Prefetch, Amcache, or user profiles are present, so no execution corroboration or cross-system identity binding is possible. The answer is therefore: account name chenwei performed both transfers as recorded; treating the two same-named accounts as one individual is unsupported inference, not a supported fact.

limitations: Absence of a binding record is a statement about the available evidence, not proof that two distinct people exist.
